newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS-Dah Sing $300 mln debt launch.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS-Dah Sing $300 mln debt launch.

text.p: Dah Sing Bank launched its US$300 million cross-border mortgage-backed security issue on Monday.
The issue, which will be listed in Luxembourg, was lead-managed by HSBC Markets and guaranteed by CAPMAC.
It paid a margin of 20 basis points over the One-month London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR).
The relatively low margin was achieved through credit enhancements.
Dah Sing Bank is the third Hong Kong entity to opt for mortgage-backed issue recently, with an arm of Sanwa Bank Ltd 8320.HK and Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd both selling off mortgages.
Sanwa International Finance Hong Kong Ltd issued US$144 million worth of mortgages in an issue of mortgage-backed floating-rate notes (FRNs) due 2017.
Sanwa's notes were priced and reoffered at par and paid a coupon of 20 basis points over three-month LIBOR until August 2007, and 45 basis points over thereafter.

Hongkong Telecom's HK$800 million mortgage-backed FRN matures in 2019, and were priced and reoffered at par, paying an an interest margin of 60 basis points over the one-month Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate (HIBOR).
Both Sanwa International and Hongkong Telecom also had their issues credit enhanced.
The long-awaited HK$6.5 billion syndicated four-year loan for redevelopment of the former Shiu Wing steel mill site in Hong Kong should be out this week, bankers said.
The loan will be launched through a special-purpose company, Arrowtown Assets Ltd, and will be guaranteed by Swire Properties Ltd and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd, they said.
It pays a margin of 50 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate, they said.
Chase Manhattan Asia, Hang Seng Bank, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, Banque Nationale de Paris, Sanwa Bank and Standard Chartered Bank are coordinating arrangers for the loan.
Chase Manhattan Asia and Hang Seng Bank are bookrunners.
